alice.g: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel bump (v1.12) we saw a ~22% drop in prefix-cache hit rate for the chat workload on the 8xA100 pool. Notable at 95th token latency slices.

benji: oof. did the bump change KV layout or the serialization path?

alice.g: quick summary from profiling: hit-rate pre-bump ~71.3% -> post-bump ~49.8%. CPU time spent in key-gen went up ~2.1x. NVTX traces point to more time in the tokenizer normalization step right before keying.

sasha_r: can you paste the small repro of the key-gen? curious if whitespace / canonicalization changed.

alice.g: sure — here's the snippet we run for keying (simplified):
```python
# canonicalize prompt -> generate key
normalized = re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", prompt.strip()).lower()
meta = json.dumps(tool_args, sort_keys=True)
key = sha256((model_id + '|' + normalized + '|' + meta).encode()).hexdigest()
```
Post-bump the tokenizer returns slightly different token boundaries for contractions (e.g., "don't" -> ["do", "n't"]) which changes normalized string length and increases CPU in our normalization layer (we call `.lower()` + regex on the detokenized text).

benji: ah — so it's tokenizer behavior, not kernel arithmetic. Did the kernel change the tokenizer binary or the tokenization config?

alice.g: kernel bump included a tokenizer patch (fast-tokenizer v0.9.3) that changes join/detokenize heuristics. The runtime used the detokenize -> normalize -> key pipeline instead of deriving key from token ids, so small detokenize diffs blow up keys.

sasha_r: two immediate options: (1) pin tokenizer version used for key-gen (derive a stable canonicalizer binary) or (2) switch keying to use token ids + model_version suffix so detokenize invariances don't matter. Option 2 needs careful handling for tool/function fields.

benji: +1 for token-id based keying long term. Short-term we should roll forward a hotfix: normalize via token-id fingerprint to avoid detokenize. e.g. `key = sha256(model+'|'+','.join(map(str,token_ids))+'|'+meta)`

alice.g: agreed. Quick mitigation we rolled to prod last night: pin tokenizers to v0.9.2 for the keying worker group and rewarm prefixes for high-traffic cohorts. infra-bot reported the deploy:

infra-bot: deploy to runtime-keyers group started by @alice.g — rollout 8/8 hosts — status: success :white_check_mark:

benji: did the hotfix recover hit rate?

alice.g: partial recovery — back to ~68% on the rollup within 2 hours. But we still see some cohorts at ~61% (likely requests with tool args ordering differences).

sasha_r: tool args ordering... are we still JSON-dumping metadata without canonical sort in every codepath?

alice.g: one of the older callers uses unordered dicts coming from a GO microservice that doesn't sort keys before we serialize. I proposed adding a metadata normalizer that always does a stable sort + removes default-empty fields before we include meta in key.

benji: that's good. Also add a small bloom filter in front of key-gen to cheaply detect obvious collisions / canonicalization mismatches so we can capture metrics without producing misses.

sasha_r: for the longer term: plan to (a) move to token-id + model+tokenizer-version key, (b) add an explicit schema for function/tool args with ordered fields when they matter, and (c) record both legacy_key and tokenid_key in traces for a couple weeks to measure divergence.

alice.g: plan sounds good. I'll file a tiny RFC and an A/B rollout plan: stage 1 = pin tokenizer for keyers + meta canonicalizer (hotfix), stage 2 = token-id keying opt-in flag, stage 3 = full switch after 2 weeks of divergence <1.5%.

benji: +1. please include a regression test that fuzzes detokenize/retokenize cycles and asserts stable keys for semantically identical prompts.

alice.g: will do. adding tasks now and will ping ops for a controlled warmup (cohort-by-cohort) — thanks all :sparkles:
